content.text: They delighted fans, who revelled all day and long into the night, with classics from their back catalogue, as well as paying a touching tribute to the late Liverpool player Diogo Jota during the performance of Live Forever.
The song written in Diogo Jota's honour showcased the deep love Liverpool fans had for him.

On an emotional evening, a heartfelt rendition of Portugal's national anthem was followed by an impeccably observed minute's silence before kick-off, during which a black-and-white image of Jota was displayed on the big stadium screens in Bern.

Jota's final and 65th goal for Liverpool, a quintessential poacher’s strike against Everton before the Kop in April, now serves as a shining symbol - a cherished memory for fans who can reflect on the joy of experiencing it with him.
Liverpool head coach Arne Slot has also released a statement following the tragic passing of Diogo Jota and his brother Andre Silva.
